newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-LEWIS GETS GREEN LIGHT, SLAMS METS FOR GIANTS VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-LEWIS GETS GREEN LIGHT, SLAMS METS FOR GIANTS VICTORY.

text.p: Mark Lewis made the most of his "green light" by crushing a grand slam homer in the seventh inning that gave the San Francisco Giants a 5-2 victory Tuesday over the New York Mets.
The Mets scored twice in the first and held that lead until the Giants exploded in the seventh for all their runs.

Lewis faced a 3-0 count against sinkerball reliever Greg McMichael (7-8) with the bases loaded and two outs and the score 2-1. With a walk good enough to bring in the game-tying run, Lewis took the next pitch for a strike.

Rather than issue a "take" sign to try again to coax a walk, Giants manager Dusty Baker let Lewis swing away and the third baseman took advantage of the green light by lining a fat fastball over the left-centre field wall.

"I'd been in that situation a lot over the last couple of weeks and I haven't come through," Lewis said. "I was just saying to myself 'this has to be it.' I told myself I was going to make him get the ball up. If he would've thrown the ball up by my head, I probably would've swung at it."
Shawn Estes pitched eight-plus innings to improve his record to 14-4.

"I threw some good pitches and they either fouled them off or they were just too low," said McMichael said. "I definitely made enough pitches to get out of the inning, but I got behind to Lewis and I got the ball up in the zone."
The Giants maintained their one-game lead over second-place Los Angeles in the NL West.

At Florida, Moises Alou hit a pair of homers and Alex Fernandez allowed one run over eight innings as the Florida Marlins snapped a three-game losing streak with a 7-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
Fernandez improved to 12-8, and Bobby Bonilla also contributed a homer for Florida, who moved a half-game ahead of the Mets in the chase for the NL wild-card spot.
In Houston, Shane Reynolds allowed one run and six hits over seven innings and Craig Biggio homered, tripled and drove in two runs as the red-hot Houston Astros defeated the St. Louis Cardinals 5-4.
Reynolds (6-6) walked none and struck out five.

Trailing 5-3 entering the bottom of the ninth, the Cardinals got the tying run on base. A single by Delino DeShields scored Willie McGee but relief ace Billy Wagner regrouped and struck out Royce Clayton to end the game and post his 19th save in 22 opportunities.
Houston extended their lead in the Central to six games over Pittsburgh and St Louis.

In Los Angeles, Pedro Astacio allowed one run and five hits over 7 1/3 innings as the Los Angeles Dodgers defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 3-1 to complete a two-game sweep and extend their winning streak to five games.

Astacio improved to 7-7. The Dodgers got all the runs they would need in the first against Pirates starter Steve Cooke (8-10). Eric Karros had an RBI groundout and Raul Mondesi added a two-out single that plated Mike Piazza.
At Colorado, Pedro Martinez threw a five-hitter for his major league-leading ninth complete game and Rondell White drove in a pair of runs as the Montreal Expos blanked the Colorado Rockies 3-0.

Martinez (12-5), who also tied Astros ace Darryl Kile for the major-league lead with four shutouts, walked one and struck out 13, marking the 10th time this year he has fanned 10 or more. The righty lowered his ERA to an NL-best 1.80.
"He's now entering the age where he's a man," Expos manager Felipe Alou said of Martinez.

"He's got three major-league pitches and all have quality. He throws 96 or 97 miles per hour and batters know that. He's got, I believe, the best changeup in the league. The curveball is sweet. I don't know what the strategy is against a guy like that."

In Atlanta, Kevin Millwood won as a starter for the first time in his major-league career as Andruw Jones hit a two-run homer and scored twice, leading the Atlanta Braves to a 7-2 victory over the road-weary Chicago Cubs.
Millwood (2-2) gave up a run and eight hits over six innings.
The Cubs fell to 0-6 on their seven-game trip and are 16-40 on the road this season.

In San Diego, Tyler Green recorded his first win in the major leagues in over two years and Kevin Stocker slugged a three-run in the second inning as the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Padres 6-5 completing a sweep of their two-game set.
Green (1-1) held the Padres to two runs and four hits over six innings.
Ricky Bottalico surrendered Steve Finley's two-run homer with two outs in the ninth, but came back to get Wally Joyner to bounce to shortstop for his 19th save.
